title: State’s 6061 All-Road V2 Goes Aero, Internal, and Transmission-Ready for $1,499.99
content:
State Bicycle Co. built its name on affordable, good-looking fixies. Now, they’re known for an entire fleet of well-spec’d, affordable bicycles available in all disciplines. Lately, they’ve been knockin’ it outta the park with the insanely good deal on their new 4130 Trail bike. It’s not a big stretch to see the brand throw a T47 BB and UDH at a sub-$1,500 gravel bike. Meet the new All-Road V2.

The new 6061 All-Road V2 is available now through State’s website at $1,499.99. State says it’s the fastest and best-equipped gravel bike it has built for under $1,500, and that it’s a generational change over V1, not a refresh. New frame, new standards, new drivetrain, new brakes, new wheels. That’s a lot of “new” for a bike that still costs less than a high end set of carbon wheels.

Let’s go over the details, yeah?

Aero-ish & Hidden-Hoses

The new frame is double-butted 6061 aluminum, shaped using the same aero profiles as State’s best-selling 6061 track frames. State says the profiled tubes and fully hidden cables cut the drag. An ID52 head tube routes hoses from the bar through the headset and down the steerer. The finish is a painted “anodized” look, which is a fun bit of wordplay, but State says the aluminum shows through the paint, so take that for what it’s worth.

The Standards Stuff

There are two modern standards that come with the new All-Road frame. First, there’s the T47 threaded bottom bracket, which means no press-fit creaking and any shop can service it with normal tools. Second, there’s the UDH hanger.

The tire clearance maxes out at 55mm in either 700c or 650b. It comes with 29 x 2.0″ Continental tires. The wheels have a 25mm internal width, 30mm depth, 32 spokes, and brass nipples, and they ship tubeless-ready, taped and valved. Just add sealant.

Drivetrain & Brakes

The 12-speed drivetrain uses an 11-46t cassette. The derailleur is rated to 50T, though, so if you decide you want a mullet setup down the road, it is possible. The aero crank runs a solid narrow-wide 42T 7075 ring on forged 6061 arms with a 29mm spindle.

Stopping comes from carbon levers and a full hydraulic system with 160mm rotors front and rear.

All-Road V2 Geometry

The new All-Road V2’s chainstays are 445mm with 73mm of BB drop for stability at speed and on loose descents. State says the 50mm fork offset and taller tire put trail at roughly 73 to 78mm on the small sizes and about 68mm on Medium and Large.

Head angles are size-specific: 70° on XS and S and 71.5° on M and L, which is a nice touch when many brands, especially at this price, run one angle across the whole range.

Reach grew 5 to 10mm over V1, mostly on the bigger sizes, but State rebalanced stem lengths so fit stays close to V1. Crank arms and stems scale with size too, so smaller riders aren’t getting a shrunk-down big bike.

Wheel Upgrades

If the stock wheels aren’t enough, State offers two options: DT Swiss G1800 Spline for +$450 (650b or 700c), or Zipp 303 XPLR S carbon for +$1,000 (700c only, MSRP $1,500). Here’s a heads-up on the Zipp: it’s hookless, so it can run tubeless tires only.

State’s All-Road V2 Retail & Detail

Retail: $1,499

  • Colors: Liquid Emerald (green), Chrome Red, Metallic Smoke (graphite)
  • Sizes: XS 48cm, S 51cm, M 54cm, L 58cm
  • Wheel size: 700c or 650b, selected at checkout, same frame and clearance
  • Frame: Double-butted 6061 aluminum, aero-profiled tubes, painted “anodized” finish
  • Routing: Fully internal through ID52 head tube, down the steerer
  • Bottom bracket: T47 threaded
  • Rear end: UDH, direct-mount for SRAM Transmission derailleurs
  • Max tire clearance: 700c x 55mm or 650b x 55mm
  • Stock tires: Continental 29 x 2.0 (model unspecified)
  • Wheels: 25mm internal width, 30mm deep, 32 spokes, brass nipples, tubeless-ready (taped and valved, sealant not included)
  • Crankset: Aero, solid narrow-wide 42T 7075 ring, forged 6061 arms, 29mm spindle, 49.7mm chainline
  • Drivetrain: 12-speed, 11-46t cassette, derailleur rated to 50T
  • Gearing: 418% range, 0.91:1 low gear (State says)
  • Brakes: Full hydraulic, carbon levers, 160mm rotors front and rear
  • Saddle: 150mm trail saddle
  • Geometry: 445mm chainstays, 73mm BB drop, 50mm fork offset
  • Head angle: 70° (XS, S), 71.5° (M, L)
  • Trail: ~73-78mm (small sizes), ~68mm (M, L), per State
  • Fit changes vs. V1: Reach up 5-10mm, stems rebalanced, size-scaled cranks and stems
  • Wheel upgrades: DT Swiss G1800 Spline (+$450, 700c or 650b); Zipp 303 XPLR S carbon (+$1,000, 700c only, hookless, tubeless only, 50 psi max, approved tires only)

On paper, this looks to be a serious rethink of an entry-level gravel bike. The frame standards come in way above the price, and the size-specific geometry is the kind of detail usually saved for the pricier bikes. In my opinion, State just keeps doing things right, and you should probably take notice.
